title: Rift Vector
atomic_requirements: Movement clamps the ship centre to x=16..304 and y=32..192 logical pixels, normalizes diagonals, and uses speeds 80, 96, 112 and 128 px/s for speed levels 0..3.
Each distinct fire press emits exactly one 1-damage vulcan shot immediately, ignores operating-system key repeats and produces no automatic vulcan shots while held.
A continuous fire hold starts charging at 0.30 s, reaches wave tiers 1, 2 and 3 at total hold times 0.60, 1.10 and 1.80 s, and emits no wave before release.
Fire release below 0.60 s emits no wave, while release at the three tier boundaries emits exactly one piercing beam of damage 8, 20 or 48 and collision height 8, 16 or 24 px respectively.
A wave damages each intersected enemy once, pierces at least three aligned enemies, stops at solid terrain and empties the BEAM gauge after release.
The first laser crystal creates a level-1 Force and every later crystal raises its level by one up to level 3 while setting the red, blue or yellow weapon by crystal colour.
A returning or detached Force touching the ship's front half attaches front and touching its rear half attaches rear, with attached laser fire directed away from that side.
A Force press launches an attached pod across the playfield at 200 px/s, and a second press recalls a detached pod towards the ship at 160 px/s.
After launch the detached Force holds x=264 when the ship is left of x=160 or x=56 otherwise, mirrors ship Y at up to 160 px/s, and remains indestructible while blocking enemy bullets.
Each fire press gives a detached Force level-1 one forward bullet, level-2 bullets at plus and minus 30 degrees, or level-3 those two bullets plus vertical up and down bullets.
Each fire press with an attached red Force emits twin lasers which become an intertwining helix at level 3, and rear attachment reverses their direction.
Each fire press with an attached blue Force emits beams at 0 and plus/minus 45 degrees relative to attachment direction, reflecting off terrain normals at most twice before expiring after 1.2 s.
Each fire press with an attached yellow Force emits up/down plumes which follow the contacted terrain boundary in attachment direction for at most 0.8 s without passing through terrain.
At most two bit pickups occupy offsets (0,20) and (0,-20), cannot be destroyed, block enemy bullets, and fire one red bolt per fire press only while red is equipped.
A missile pickup enables two homing missiles per fire press subject to a shared 0.8 s cooldown, with nearest-live-enemy targeting and maximum turn rate 180 degrees/s.
Speed pickups increase speed level by one and cannot raise it beyond level 3.
Each killed carrier drops its scheduled pickup, with carriers every 12 s of scrolling and stage-relative drops at 12/24/36/48/60/72 s of red/blue/bit/yellow/missile/speed.
One unshielded collision kills the ship, subtracts one life from an initial three lives and restarts at scroll 0 or the reached 1152 px checkpoint after a 1.0 s death interval.
Death retains an acquired Force at level 1 attached front but removes colour weapon, bits, missiles and speed, and gives 2.0 s flashing respawn invulnerability.
A continued run starts with three lives at the last reached checkpoint and score zero while retaining the saved hi-score and acquired-Force level-1 death economy.
Kills award drone 100, fighter 200, carrier 500, turret 300, worm segment 150, mine 50, dop 250 and crawler 200 points exactly once per stage spawn identifier, even after checkpoint replay.
Boss defeat awards 5000+1000 times the stage number, and clearing a stage without a death since its first entry awards another 10000 points.
A new hi-score is saved immediately with sys.save, restored after application restart, and never reduced by death, continue or a malformed save file.
Stages 1 through 10 each scroll 1920 px at 24 px/s before a boss lock, contain a checkpoint at 60 percent scroll and advance only when that stage's boss is defeated.

Across stages 1 through 10 base spawn interval decreases from 2.40 to 1.50 s, hostile bullet speed rises from 36 to 63 px/s and boss HP rises from 120 to 300, with at most 10 simultaneous hostile bullets and 8 ordinary enemies.
The bottom y=0..24 HUD displays 1P score, HI score, BEAM charge, lives and stage number without covering the y=24..200 playfield.
Pause freezes movement, charge, spawning, boss clocks, cooldowns and scrolling, and resume cancels held fire without releasing a wave.
Enter starts from title, advances a cleared stage or continues from game over, and defeating the stage-10 Overmind enters victory with the final score.
Every boss telegraphs damaging attacks for at least 0.60 s and provides the stage table's timed weak-point opening; no boss requires a collected weapon to defeat.
The Linux release runs on both Vulkan and OpenGL using the wired application manifest, while the web release loads and runs its WebGL engine with the same keyboard and bot-message controls.
All shipped visual assets use the declared 16-colour art family, nearest-neighbour display and original biomechanical designs with a visual-cohesion score of at least 70.
Audio unlock follows a real start gesture on web, charge audio stops on release/death/pause, and only the seven allowed STUDIO_TELEMETRY event types enter that channel.
In test mode the simulation advances only through test_advance and reports state through test_spawn_report.
